title: feat(core): define a categorized error taxonomy
problem: `DevkitError` has five broad variants, so callers cannot distinguish retryable transport failures from deterministic decode failures in a stable way.
why: A precise taxonomy lets the CLI map errors to exit codes, lets the RPC layer decide what is retryable, and prevents fragile string matching.
context: `DevkitError` currently has Decode, Encode, InvalidInput, Config, and Io.
scope: Introduce a stable category enum (Input, Decode, Encode, Config, Transport, NotFound, Limit, Internal)
Keep the existing variants as constructors that set a category
Document which categories are retryable
out_of_scope: Changing public function signatures beyond error construction.
guidance: Prefer additive change; keep the human message readable.
Make retryability a method on the error, not a match in the client.
acceptance: Retryability is derived from the category and tested
tests: Unit tests for every category and retry decision
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(core): add shared Severity and Confidence models
problem: There is no shared severity/confidence representation for analysis output.
why: Security and tooling output must use one honest scale instead of ad-hoc strings.
context: No analysis layer exists yet, so this must be defined before findings.
scope: Add Severity (info..critical) and Confidence (low..high) enums with ordering and parsing
Document the meaning of each level
guidance: Mirror the widely used model and keep parsing strict.
acceptance: Enums parse, order, and serialize stably
tests: Parsing, ordering, and serde round-trip tests
security: Confidence must never be inflated; document that.
docs: Document in ARCHITECTURE and a future security guide.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(core): add a versioned output envelope for machine-readable commands
problem: JSON output has no envelope or version, so consumers cannot evolve safely.
why: A stable envelope with a schema version is a prerequisite for stable machine output.
scope: Wrap JSON output in `{ schema_version, tool, command, data }`
Apply it consistently across commands
guidance: Keep the envelope tiny and additive.
acceptance: Every JSON command emits the envelope
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: refactor(core): add validation primitives for untrusted strings
problem: Validation of lengths, encodings, and character sets is scattered and duplicated.
why: Centralized primitives make untrusted-input handling consistent and auditable.
context: Decoders and config loaders each validate differently.
scope: Add small helpers for bounded length, ASCII/base32 checks, and non-empty trimmed input
Use them across crates
acceptance: Helpers are used by at least the strkey and config paths
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: test(core): add deterministic snapshot tests for core types
problem: Serialization of core types is asserted piecewise, so shape drift can slip through.
why: Snapshots make output changes explicit and reviewable.
scope: Add snapshot tests for Network, OutputFormat, and error categories
guidance: Store small golden files under tests/ and document the update procedure.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): implement JSON-RPC request construction
problem: The transport receives a method and params, but no component builds or validates a JSON-RPC 2.0 request envelope.
why: Centralizing request construction guarantees correct ids, version, and params for every method.
scope: Add a `Request` builder producing a JSON-RPC 2.0 object
Add a `Response` parser that distinguishes result and error
guidance: Keep ids monotonic per client and testable.
acceptance: Requests and responses parse and are validated
tests: Unit tests for request/response shapes and error mapping
security: Reject malformed responses with structured errors.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): distinguish Horizon and RPC data sources
problem: The toolkit does not distinguish Horizon from Stellar RPC, although they serve different data and retention.
why: Choosing the wrong source yields missing or mislabeled data; the docs are explicit that RPC is not an indexer.
context: Stellar RPC retains a bounded recent window; Horizon provides indexing.
scope: Model a data-source choice in configuration
Document what each supports and warn when a request targets an unsupported source
guidance: Keep RPC first; make Horizon explicitly future work.
acceptance: Source selection is modeled and documented
security: Endpoint validation applies to both sources.
docs: Add an RPC guide section on sources.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): add cursor-based pagination for list methods
problem: List methods that return a cursor have no pagination helper.
why: Pagination is required to retrieve more than one page safely and deterministically.
context: Pagination for events is tracked separately; this provides a shared helper.
scope: Add a bounded paginator over a cursor-returning method
Enforce a maximum page count and total size
tests: Unit tests with mocked multi-page responses
security: Bound loops to prevent resource exhaustion.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): add a typed JSON-RPC error taxonomy
problem: JSON-RPC error objects are not modeled, so callers cannot react to specific codes (for example not found or rate limited).
why: Typed RPC errors enable correct retry and user messaging.
context: Responses are parsed but errors are not classified.
scope: Model code, message, and data
Map known codes to error categories and retryability
out_of_scope: Server-side error semantics beyond the documented set.
guidance: Preserve the raw code for diagnostics.
acceptance: Known codes map to categories; unknown codes are preserved
tests: Unit tests per known code and an unknown code
security: Do not trust error data blindly; bound its size.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): handle rate limiting and Retry-After
problem: Rate-limit responses are not handled distinctly.
why: Correct backoff on rate limits avoids bans and failed CI runs.
context: Retry policy exists; Retry-After is not parsed.
scope: Detect rate-limit responses and honor Retry-After within a cap
Surface a clear error when the cap is exceeded
guidance: Never sleep unboundedly; cap total wait.
acceptance: Rate limits are detected and bounded backoff applied
tests: Unit tests with a mocked rate-limit response
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): add connection reuse and pool configuration
problem: The live transport (once added) would open a new connection per call unless pooling is configured.
why: Connection reuse materially reduces latency for multi-call workflows.
context: The live transport is tracked separately.
scope: Configure connection reuse and pool size in the transport
Expose conservative defaults
performance: This is the optimization; measure it.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: test(rpc): add a local integration test server
problem: Live transport behavior can only be tested against mocks, not a real HTTP server.
why: A local server exercises request framing, status codes, and redirects without external network access.
scope: Add a loopback JSON-RPC test server used by integration tests
Cover success, error, malformed, and redirect responses
out_of_scope: Testing against real public endpoints in CI.
guidance: Bind only to loopback; never depend on the internet.
acceptance: Integration tests run offline and deterministically
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.
